items.title: 54270_Doc Cheatham oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Now, this is now 1939, you were listening to people like Louie Armstrong and Freddie Keppard? [INTERVIEWEE] Uh-huh.

ctx.x: And jazz. He had a great band, it was too great, it was too good. That's why it didn't last. It was just too good.

items.title: 54270_Doc Cheatham oral history interview
items.q: So then I went to hear Kneppard Freddie Kappel

ctx.x: With Erskine Tate. Then that was my first time hearing of New Orleans musicians, I never heard of New Orleans musicians before. So then I went to hear Kneppard Freddie Kappel, and Bob Shoffner and then I got interested in that type of music and that's why I threw the saxophone away. I said the trumpet is more beautiful than saxophone and I just decided to ditch the saxophone altogether. During the time I was with Al, though, at the Dreamland I played saxophone

and then I started to play cornet, which he liked my cornet playing also, better. But he had a cornet player in the band recorded with at that time and we recall it was Ma Rainey there with Wynn Al Williams, I was playing soprano saxophone.
